title: step: architect lazy-loaded Vault tree design
description: Use the architect workflow before implementation. Compare at least two designs for lazy-loading folder children, including a normalized tree state model versus patching nested children in place. Name the canonical data shape for directory load state, loaded children, pagination cursor, stale poll refresh, and errors.
acceptance_criteria: Design records the chosen data shape, API contract changes, polling reconciliation strategy, TreeList integration approach, and migration path from the existing recursive snapshot. If architect is skipped, notes must say architect skipped with a concrete reason.
notes:
architect workflow used. Design candidates compared normalized state against nested child patching, then an independent reviewer approved the synthesized direction.

Chosen architecture: normalized Vault tree state, delivered through a compatibility adapter that can ingest the current recursive VaultTreeNode[] snapshot.

Canonical state shape: nodesByPath, rootIds, directoriesByPath, expandedPaths, selectedPath, treeMeta.

Directory load variants: unloaded, loading, loaded, refreshing, loadingMore, error. Loaded data carries childIds, nextCursor, truncated, loadedAtMs or equivalent, loadedPageCount or equivalent. Request-bearing states carry requestId. Refresh/error states carry stale or preserved prior data so a failed folder refresh does not clear visible children.

API contract: add a typed web fetchVaultEntries({ path, cursor, limit? }) helper and VaultEntriesResponse with path, entries, source, truncated, next_cursor. Extend BFF GET /api/vault/entries to accept cursor and optional limit if chosen by implementation, then forward cursor through backend-runtime listVaultEntries to BackendRuntimeService.listVault and Brain RPC vault.list. Preserve ACL enforcement and fail-closed behavior.

Polling reconciliation: do not blindly replace all visible tree state. Reconcile root metadata from /api/vault/tree, preserve loaded directory children when paths still exist, refresh expanded loaded directories via /api/vault/entries, mark stale on transient failures, clear only on auth/ACL-deny class failures, and ignore obsolete request ids.

TreeList integration: add vaultStateToTreeItems or equivalent adapter. Use synthetic rows for unloaded/loading/error/load-more states rather than fake VaultTreeNode files. Inspect Astryx TreeList for a real expansion callback. Prefer that if available; otherwise use folder row activation as the first implementation and file follow-up if chevron-only lazy loading is required.

Migration sequence: first normalize existing recursive snapshots and keep current /api/vault/tree behavior. Second add /entries cursor support and lazy folder expansion. Third add shallow initial tree mode only after the lazy path works. Keep the 500-node recursive budget and existing honesty banner until the later copy/docs bead updates user-facing language.
close_reason: Architected lazy Vault tree design. Evidence: two read-only candidate designs compared normalized state vs nested patching; reviewer approved normalized-state target with compatibility adapter, API contract, polling rules, TreeList plan, and migration sequence recorded in notes.

title: feature: lazy-load Vault tree folders
description: Context: Portal currently builds a bounded recursive Vault tree through GET /api/vault/tree. The tree only contains metadata, but recursively enumerating every folder still creates host, relay, BFF, and browser pressure. The current 500-node cap avoids unbounded fan-out, but users can miss nested files in large vaults. Goal: keep the bounded initial tree, then fetch folder children on demand through GET /api/vault/entries so users can navigate large project folders without raising the global recursive tree budget.
acceptance_criteria: Vault keeps a bounded initial tree and no longer requires every file to fit under VAULT_TREE_MAX_NODES to be discoverable. Expanding a directory fetches missing children through the entries endpoint with ACL enforcement, pagination or an explicit partial-folder state, loading and error UI, and tests covering BFF, web state, and browser behavior.
notes: 2026-07-29: Lazy Vault tree implementation and verification are complete through lp-ypx.13. lp-ypx.14 has a PR-ready description in its notes but is blocked because active instructions forbid git operations (branch/commit/push/open PR).
close_reason: Lazy Vault tree folder loading implemented, verified, and merged via PR #164 (5069f0a).

Hermes: root npm react-router/postcss/dompurify, website critical websocket-driver plus ws/undici/etc., Photon sidecar OpenTelemetry/protobuf, whatsapp bridge body-parser, Python cryptography and Pillow. Prefer upgrading/removing vulnerable packages; where impossible, document reachability and mitigations.

title: P1 security: harden Hermes plugin import, image fetch, env perms, and tirith install
description: Hermes follow-up hardening: model-provider plugins under HERMES_HOME auto-import outside the normal enabled-plugin allowlist; image-generation URL caching uses raw requests.get without SSRF validation; .env updates preserve unsafe existing modes; tirith auto-install accepts latest release with cosign optional. Move these controls to the plugin/config/network/supply-chain boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] User model-provider plugins require the same allowlist/enablement policy before import.
- [ ] Agent file writes to HERMES_HOME/plugins/** are blocked or require explicit approval.
- [ ] Image URL caching validates scheme, DNS/IP, redirects, content-length, byte cap, and image magic bytes.
- [ ] Private, loopback, link-local, and metadata IP targets are blocked for provider-returned URLs.
- [ ] .env secret writes clamp unsafe world/group permissions to a safe maximum outside documented managed modes.
- [ ] tirith auto-install is pinned, cosign-required, or explicitly opt-in.
- [ ] Targeted Hermes plugin, file-safety, image-fetch, env-mode, and tirith tests pass.

title: P1 security: harden lanyard-agent email, Teams, exports, and health endpoints
description: Agent channel and local-data hardening items: email reply template permits CR/LF header injection; Teams stores inbound serviceUrl and later POSTs with a bearer token; history export files use process umask and redaction defaults off; /ready returns channel/session details if health bind is exposed. Apply boundary validation and local file-permission hardening.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Email header values reject or sanitize CR/LF across Subject, From, To, In-Reply-To, and References.
- [ ] Email address and message-id handling uses a safe formatter/parser or equivalent tests.
- [ ] Teams serviceUrl requires HTTPS, approved Bot Framework hosts, and no private/link-local targets before storing.
- [ ] Conversation references are stored only from authenticated/prevalidated activities.
- [ ] History export directories/files are 0700/0600 or equivalent, and systemd export unit sets UMask=0077.
- [ ] Export redaction has an explicit production choice.
- [ ] /ready sensitive details are redacted or gated when health bind is non-localhost.
- [ ] Relevant adapter, export, and gateway health tests pass.

title: P1 security: stream and cap Office callback downloads
description: Office callback SSRF controls are mostly present, but the fetch path calls response.arrayBuffer before enforcing max size when Content-Length is absent. A compromised or misconfigured allowlisted Document Server can force BFF to buffer a large body. Stream the callback download with a hard byte cap, timeout, redirect-target rechecks, and clear metrics. Also review nonce-in-query exposure and move callback authentication out of URL params if ONLYOFFICE supports it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Callback download reads in chunks and aborts once maxBytes is exceeded.
- [ ] Missing Content-Length no longer permits unbounded buffering.
- [ ] Fetch timeout and maximum read duration are enforced.
- [ ] Redirect handling revalidates every target host/IP.
- [ ] Tests simulate no Content-Length oversized body and prove bounded memory behavior.
- [ ] Callback URL nonce exposure is either removed or documented with a residual-risk decision.
- [ ] BFF office callback/download tests pass.
notes:
Implemented stream/cap Office callback fetcher (lp-p37.9).

title: P1 security: harden portal service boundaries and secrets
description: Several portal boundary risks remain: control-plane opens non-health routes in development when no service token is set, BFF has production fallback values for RELAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN and SESSION_SECRET, Google OAuth redirect URI uses the raw Host header, and relay internal JSON body reads are unbounded with plain string token comparison. Harden these at config/network boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Control-plane fails closed unless production token is configured or explicit local-dev open mode is set.
- [ ] BFF production rejects missing or dev-placeholder relayInternalToken and sessionSecret.
- [ ] OAuth redirect origin is derived from canonical tenant/app host allowlist, not raw Host.
- [ ] Relay internal endpoints cap JSON body size and abort early on oversized bodies.
- [ ] Internal token comparisons use constant-time comparison where practical.
- [ ] Tests cover misconfigured production env, dev local override, Host spoofing, and oversized internal request bodies.
- [ ] Control-plane and relay test suites pass.
notes:
Implemented on beads/lp-p37.8-p1-security-harden-portal-service-bounda @ e2514c2. PR: https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/147

Acceptance evidence:

- BFF prod rejects RELAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN / SESSION_SECRET placeholders: config.ts + control-plane-service-auth.test
- OAuth allowlist origin: oauth-redirect.ts + app.ts; Host spoofing tests
- Relay body cap + constant-time token: internal-http.ts + internal-http-security.test
- CP suite 130/130, relay 100/100, BFF security 20/20

title: P1 security: enforce RBAC/admin authorization on portal settings mutations
description: BFF settings fallback routes require authentication and CSRF but not RBAC/admin permission before reading or mutating Hermes settings. Any authenticated user can toggle skills, crons, MCP servers, or active model when live Hermes config is writable. Add explicit RBAC/admin/settings permission checks before both Brain RPC and fallback branches. Prefer routing mutations through BackendRuntime/Brain RPC with host-side authorization when available.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] GET settings snapshot permission is explicitly defined and tested.
- [ ] PATCH settings skills/crons/MCP/models requires admin or explicit settings permission.
- [ ] Permission checks run before fallback file writes and before Brain RPC delegation.
- [ ] Member/contributor users without permission receive 403 and no file mutation.
- [ ] Admin/settings-permitted users can mutate only allowed settings.
- [ ] Tests cover fixture fallback and live Hermes-home write paths.
- [ ] DB-backed BFF settings integration tests pass.
notes:
Implemented settings RBAC on BFF routes. commit=15a5fb9da67146c1f9f0bc5fce0883a5ff48d802 branch=beads/lp-p37.7-p1-security-enforce-rbac-admin-authoriza PR=https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/142 (draft). Policy: settings.read=authenticated session; settings.manage=admin or explicit settings-manager role labels. Checks run before Brain RPC and fixture/Hermes writes. Tests: rbac-settings 6/6, settings.integration 9/9, brain-rpc.integration 22/22 (incl. contributor 403 before settings.patch).
